title: 2011 HMMT November Guts Problem 32
statement:
Find all real numbers \(x\) satisfying

\[x^{9}+\frac{9}{8} x^{6}+\frac{27}{64} x^{3}-x+\frac{219}{512}=0\]

solutions.text:
\(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{13}}{4}\) Note that we can re-write the given equation as

\[\sqrt[3]{x-\frac{3}{8}}=x^{3}+\frac{3}{8}\]

Furthermore, the functions of \(x\) on either side, we see, are inverses of each other and increasing. Let \(f(x)=\sqrt[3]{x-\frac{3}{8}}\). Suppose that \(f(x)=y=f^{-1}(x)\). Then, \(f(y)=x\). However, if \(x<y\), we have \(f(x)>f(y)\), contradicting the fact that \(f\) is increasing, and similarly, if \(y<x\), we have \(f(x)<f(y)\), again a contradiction. Therefore, if \(f(x)=f^{-1}(x)\) and both are increasing functions in \(x\), we require \(f(x)=x\). This gives the cubic

\[x^{3}-x+\frac{3}{8}=0 \rightarrow\left(x-\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(x^{2}+\frac{1}{2} x-\frac{3}{4}\right)=0,\]

giving \(x=\frac{1}{2}, \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{13}}{4}\).
